topic: January is the international deadline, but not an IB candidate's
text:
Sweden runs two admissions rounds and they are not two chances at the same thing. The first opens in October and closes on 15 January; it is aimed at applicants from abroad and carries the most English-taught programmes. The second closes on 15 April, and the authority says many English-taught programmes are no longer available in it.

For a May 2027 IB candidate the order is reversed. University Admissions says that if you have not completed your IB Diploma you should not apply to the first round, because it cannot assess you in time without the diploma. Your round is the second, with your IB results due to University Admissions by 5 July through the IB Result Service. So shortlist programmes that are still open in the second round, and treat the January round as closed to you unless a programme, like Stockholm School of Economics, says it admits on predicted grades.
attribution: University Admissions, the national admissions authority, on its key-dates page and its page for IB students
whatThisIsNot: Not a claim that the first round is closed to every IB student. A student who already holds a completed IB Diploma may apply in either round.
